He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|University of Tulsa]] and represents the [[Jamaica national basketball team|Jamaica national team]] in international competition. ==Early life== Jordan was born to parents Bryan and Faith Jordan in [[Kingston, Jamaica]], a city with just two hardwood courts, and it was not until age 16 that Jordan began playing basketball. Stephen Johnston, a former Jamaica national team captain, found a spot for Jordan at Redemption Christian Academy in [[Troy, New York]], which he attended with his sister, Jheanelle, while his parents stayed in Jamaica. However, after one semester, Bryan withdrew Jerome and Jheanelle from the school and they returned to Kingston.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/01/sports/ncaabasketball/01jordan.html|title=A 'Big, Silly Dude' Becomes a 7-Foot Force at Tulsa|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=February 28, 2010|access-date=February 28, 2010}} After graduating from [[Jamaica College]],{{cite web|url=http://jamaica-star.com/thestar/20100625/sports/sports4.html|title=NBA bound - Tulsa's Jordan drafted by Milwaukee Bucks|work=Jamaica-Star.com|date=June 25, 2010|access-date=June 25, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100630144125/http://jamaica-star.com/thestar/20100625/sports/sports4.html|archive-date=June 30, 2010}} Jordan enrolled at [[Florida Air Academy]] in [[Melbourne, Florida]]. However, he was ineligible to play in 2005–06 due to an academic transfer rule.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=4944913|title=Seven-footer Jordan makes name for self at Tulsa|work=ESPN.com|date=February 25, 2010|access-date=February 25, 2010}} ==College career== On April 26, 2006, Jordan signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play college basketball for the [[University of Tulsa]].{{cite web|url=http://www.tulsahurricane.com/news/2006/4/26/Tulsa_Basketball_Signs_Calvin_Walls_and_Jerome_Jordan_to_National_Letters_of_Intent.aspx|title=TULSA BASKETBALL SIGNS CALVIN WALLS AND JEROME JORDAN TO NATIONAL LETTERS-OF-INTENT|work=TulsaHurricane.com|date=April 26, 2006|access-date=March 9, 2009}} In his freshman season at [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] in 2006–07, Jordan played 23 games (10 starts) while averaging 2.7 points and 2.1 rebounds in 7.8 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.tulsahurricane.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_jerome00.html |title=Jerome Jordan bio |work=TulsaHurricane.com |access-date=March 9, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722054004/http://www.tulsahurricane.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jordan_jerome00.html |archive-date=July 22, 2012 }} In his sophomore season, Jordan was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Defensive team and All-Tournament team after a season where he finished second in the conference in [[rebounds]] and first in [[field goal percentage]] and [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]]. He also led Golden Hurricane to the [[2008 College Basketball Invitational|2008 CBI]] championship and was named the tournament MVP. In 39 games (all starts), he averaged 10.5 points, 7.9 rebounds and 3.7 blocks per game. In his junior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA first team after he earned Player of the Week honors four times.{{cite web|url=http://www.tulsahurricane.com/news/2009/3/9/Tulsa_s_Jordan_and_Uzoh_Earn_Conference_USA_Honors.aspx|title=TULSA'S JORDAN AND UZOH EARN CONFERENCE USA HONORS|work=TulsaHurricane.com|date=March 9, 2009|access-date=March 9, 2009}} He was also named to the All-Defensive team for the second straight year after his 91 blocked shots gave him the number 1 and 2 positions on the school's single-season blocked shots list. In 36 games (35 starts), he averaged 13.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game. In his senior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA second team and NABC Division I All-District 11 first team. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 15.4 points, 9.1 rebounds and 2.4 blocks in 29.8 minutes per game. He finished his career as the only player in Conference USA history to record at least 800 rebounds and 300 blocks, while setting the school and conference record for blocked shots with 333 blocks. ==Professional career== ===2010–11 season=== Jordan was selected with the 44th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On July 8, 2010, his rights were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5364816|title=Knicks get Jordan from Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=July 8, 2010|access-date=July 8, 2010}} He joined the Knicks for the 2010 NBA Summer League. Later that year, he signed with [[KK Vršac|KK Hemofarm]] of Serbia for the 2010–11 season. ===2011–12 season=== On July 29, 2011, Jordan signed with [[BC Krka]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League]].{{cite news|title=KRKA adds two, extends two |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2011-12/i/86979/5745/krka-adds-two-extends-two |access-date=July 29, 2011 |work=Eurocupbasketball.com |date=July 29, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203015418/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2011-12/i/86979/5745/krka-adds-two-extends-two |archive-date=December 3, 2013 }} Following the conclusion of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]], he returned to the United States. On December 15, 2011, Jordan signed with the New York Knicks.{{cite news|title=Knicks sign center Jerome Jordan|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8842|access-date=December 15, 2011|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 15, 2011}} During the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], he was assigned multiple times to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=2011-12 Assignments|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2011_12.html|access-date=December 18, 2012|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121111185220/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2011_12.html|archive-date=November 11, 2012}} ===2012–13 season=== On July 11, 2012, Jordan was traded, along with [[Toney Douglas]], [[Josh Harrellson]] and two future second-round draft picks, to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Marcus Camby]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-make-trades-official|title=Rockets Make Trades Official|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012}} On July 18, 2012, he was waived by the Rockets.{{cite news|title=Rockets waive Jon Leuer and Jerome Jordan|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10560|access-date=July 18, 2012|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 18, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112135427/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10560|archive-date=November 12, 2014|url-status=dead}} The next day, he joined the New York Knicks for the final two games of the 2012 NBA Summer League.{{cite news|title=2012 Summer League Statistics – Jerome Jordan|url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/players/sl_jerome_jordan/|access-date=December 18, 2012|work=NBA.com}} On September 29, 2012, Jordan signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite news | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11017 | title=Memphis Grizzlies add Michael Dunigan, Ronald Dupree, Jarrid Famous, Jerome Jordan, D.J.
